newsitem.title: GERMANY: Firm Bunds seen rangebound in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Firm Bunds seen rangebound in quiet trade.

text.p: German Bunds edged higher in early afternoon trade on Thursday as dealers predicted a day of narrow rangebound trading due to the absence of fresh economic data and the Thanksgiving holiday in the U.S.
December Bund futures were quoted at 101.49 at 1230 GMT, up 12 basis points from Wednesday's close and just below the all-time high of 101.55 reached on Wednesday.
"Sentiment remains positive," one broker said, but he added that investor interest in the cash bond market was very low.
The yield on the 10-year benchmark, 6.25 percent bond was 5.76 percent, down from 5.78 percent in late trade on Thursday.
Dealers said the market appeared to be aiming for new highs.
"But we lack impetus to climb at the moment so we may not see new highs until Monday," one dealer said.
Dealers predicted Bund futures would trade in a range between 101.30 and 101.55 and saw futures contracts on five-year Bobl bonds between 104.65 to 104.85.
The December Bobl future was quoted at 104.83 at 1230 GMT.
